Congressional Outreach

Year-round advocacy for Palestinian rights at every level of government and across party lines: members meet their own elected officials, and the committee briefs State Department and DHS officials.

Branch
Leadership · A ladder by capacity
Owning entity
AFRP (Government Affairs Committee, By-Law 8.15.1)
Shape
Committee
Built in the Hub
Plan only

Who it's for

AFRP members; the committee arranges meetings with a member's own elected officials.

The operating year

Year-round. No annual cycle is stated in the record.

The five rungs

Not stated in the record for this programme. The five rungs are hear, show up, take part, give or serve, and lead (D25).

Who runs it

The Government Affairs Committee. Advocacy positions are the Federation's, adopted through governance, not a committee's own.

Money

AFRP general fund. It may be the by-laws' 'Internships in Washington' Endowed Fund purpose; confirm.

Hand-offs

Fed by exchange-mission alumni. Feeds and is fed by the Day of Action. Advocacy is organised by district, so it relies on the consented member directory.

What it needs

From the Federation's strategy
  • Decide whether policy work fits the mission; settled in practice by its place on the Leadership branch (2019 plan)
  • Elected-official relations and a stronger advocacy voice (2025 SWOT, subcommittee tasks)
  • Government Affairs named a refresh priority (2026)
From the platform
  • Only a page, charter and plan exist; relationship records are designed to stay tightly scoped
  • Advocacy contact as one more consented, refusable channel is designed, not built

Open questions

  • Is Congressional Outreach the by-laws' 'Internships in Washington' Endowed Fund purpose, or separate money?
